name: crow

attributes.attribute: a crow goddess seen as a carrion bird
screamed over battlefields to incite warriors
prophesied doom after the battle at Mag Tuired
shown as a raven riding a horse

sources: MacCulloch, J. A. The Religion of the Ancient Celts. London: Constable, 1911, 247.
O’Sullivan, Patrick V. Irish Superstitions and Legends of Animals and Birds. Cork: Mercier, 1991, 25.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Badb was a crow goddess, often seen as a carrion bird. She screamed over the battlefield, urging the fighters to bring her more fresh flesh. Sometimes she blended with the sorrowful banshee. She wept over battlefields and might predict death by wailing before a fight or washing the clothes of the dying. That task recalls the washer at the ford. Badb worked mainly as a prophet, and the tidings she gave were grim. At Mag Tuired, the last great battle for Ireland, she spoke of the bad years ahead rather than calm times. Farmers in Ireland, up to recent times, dropped their work whenever they heard a crow cry, for the sound promised ruin. Badb may connect to the Gaulish war goddess Cathubodua. Sometimes the art showed her as a raven mounted on a horse. Tribute stones to Cathubodua stand in Haute-Savoie. The tribal name Boduogenos, meaning people of Bodua, points to her in Gaul. Black-robed women and druids may have imitated Badb in battle. When the druids' school at Anglesey was destroyed, they stood aside and cried out to drive the fighters on. Whether Badb was Celtic or pre-Celtic in origin is debated. Scholars link her bird form to an unnamed Neolithic goddess shown in that form.

okr.objective: Badb is a crow goddess who cries doom over battlefields.
